name: Setaria

project_scope.caution: Not a complete Setaria checklist; S. italica is CULTIVATED/INTRODUCED. Uninstalled S. pumila and S. viridis are comparison aids, not counted canonical cards. Nativity statuses not reaudited.

look_here_first: THIS IS ABOUT THE BRISTLES: count and measure the hairlike bristles *subtending* spikelets, not true awns. Then check whole head length/density and perennial knotty basal rhizome versus annual fibrous root.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Photograph one entire rooted plant, measure head length, then a macro with several spikelets and their bristles, the true collar ligule and any hard knotty rhizome. A dense foxtail silhouette is not enough.
priority: perennial knotty rhizomes versus annual fibrous roots
recognition.safety: For public parks, expose a rhizome only where digging is permitted; otherwise mark basal anatomy unverified and photograph another legal specimen.

comparison_lesson.memory_rule: REVERCHON = SHORT/FEW bristles. SCHEELE = LONG bottlebrush, usually ONE obvious bristle. PARVIFLORA = SHORT dense head with MANY bristles + KNOTTY RHIZOME. ITALICA = CULTIVATED annual millet.
quick_split: S. reverchonii — interrupted narrow inflorescence; most upper spikelets lack bristles, others often have only one tiny ≤2mm bristle.
S. scheelei — large perennial, long 15–35cm bottlebrush panicle, usually one conspicuous long bristle at a spikelet; often hairy broad leaves.
S. parviflora — short 2.5–7cm dense head, commonly six or seven bristles per spikelet, short hard knotty rhizomes.
S. italica — robust introduced/domesticated ANNUAL foxtail millet with heavy dense grain head, broad leaves and no perennial rhizome.
comparison_lesson.anatomy_caution: The conspicuous SETARIA bristles are reduced sterile branches; they are NOT glume/lemma awns. A spikelet can be bristleless in some positions of S. reverchonii. Compare a full panicle at several nodes.

comparison_matrix.title: Setaria — four already-installed species
rows: Often none in upper region; one very short on some branches
Narrow blades; basal blades extremely fine
Long bottlebrush + usually single long bristles
S. viridis, other escaped cereal grasses

what_to_teach_crew: A foxtail 'bristle' is not an awn: look beneath, beside and around an individual spikelet.
Take the seedhead photo SIDEWAYS with ruler; one head shows whether flowering units are dense or interrupted.
At 10×, count bristles near spikelets on several portions of one head; bristle numbers can vary.
Inspect intact crown/roots where permitted: perennial hard rhizome and annual fibrous root are not interchangeable.
Keep species uncertain if a key root or spikelet character remains unseen.
Do not harvest S. italica as local wild restoration seed.
